scope: Six sampled frames per video; not continuous audiovisual listening or a new user rating

assessment.observed_condition_response: Original/swapped/zero inputs change some poses; the general small-gesture motif remains similar.
assessment.reference_fidelity: The staircase reference's light-yellow top and grey trousers still become white/blue sportswear and a small bag in several outputs.
assessment.staircase: Small arm gestures, leg curl and local pose changes persist in both A/B and zero input; no sampled-frame evidence of a substantially richer choreography.
assessment.red_outfit: Head turn and hand/arm near face or mouth remain common across original, swapped and zero conditions; B swapped has local timing/pose differences.
assessment.shop: Mostly stationary single-arm gestures and small weight shifts across A/B original, swapped and zero; sampled frames do not establish dance-control gain.
assessment.visual_quality: No obvious gross frame corruption in sampled frames; this is not a quantified sharpness or complete visual-quality verdict.

limitations: Predicted token lengths differ and change packed layouts, so video differences cannot be attributed only to learned music semantics.
Unaligned RGB MAE is not musical adherence or pose accuracy.
One hundred updates do not establish convergence; three-hundred-update comparisons and their videos remain separate work.
Technical integrity and correct full-model deployment are not proof of successful music-to-choreography learning.
